subject: Clarify SLO tally: probe sampling during partial failover and third-party fallthrough
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observed SLO variance during failover window — request for tally rationale

Hi Marissa and Laura,

We pulled our monthly SLA report and saw a 0.8% hit to our 99.9% uptime for the 2027-02-12 maintenance window. Our internal trace shows a short partial degradation between 03:22 and 03:34 UTC where the control plane failed over to a secondary region and a proportion of requests were routed to a cached model variant.

Two questions we need clarified quickly so we can reconcile with procurement:
- Why were the four probes during 03:25–03:29 counted as full outages rather than partial degradations?
- We saw a "third-party fallthrough" tag in the ticket — can you share the logic that attributes those probe failures to Redwood versus the CDN/VPN partner?

We attached our probe log excerpt (probe-log-snippet.csv) and the support ticket that started this thread.

Appreciate a timely explanation — procurement has a closing deadline next week.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
SRE, ACME Health

[attachment: probe-log-snippet.csv]
[attachment: support-ticket-12345.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed SLO variance during failover window — request for tally rationale

Hi Alex — thanks for the logs and the clear summary. Looping Ben (accounts) and Laura (SRE) to get a combined response.

Short answer: the event was recorded as full unavailability for a subset of probes because the probe sampling interval coincided with lead-region route convergence and our automatic fallback rule kicked requests to an older model build that had an incompatible I/O handshake in that minute. That triggered our binary success/failure check for those probes.

That said, I agree the customer-facing representation of the window should reflect partial degradation rather than 100% outage. We're opening this thread to:
- Confirm attribution between Redwood runtime behavior and the CDN partner handoff,
- Produce a corrected SLO tally if our internal apportionment logic is incorrect, and
- Propose a remediation (one-time credit or adjusted lightweight SLA apportionment).

Next steps: Laura — can you validate whether the runtime logged a model-variant fallback at 03:24:30–03:30:00 UTC and whether the handshake failures are ours or from the third party? Ben — if we need to issue a credit, what's the quickest non-enterprise approval path?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observed SLO variance during failover window — request for tally rationale

Hi all,

OrbitData SRE here — we saw the same maintenance window and flagged a transient edge-auth token mismatch on our side from 03:23–03:28 UTC that caused upstream requests to retry. Those retries were proxied back to the secondary region where Redwood's runtime attempted a model variant fallback.

Key artifacts attached: a short snippet of our edge logs and our service-level event id: ORB-20270212-231. From our perspective the sequence was:
1) CDN auth failure (brief) -> 2) retries and failover to secondary region -> 3) Redwood runtime fallback to cached variant -> 4) handshake mismatch for specific payloads.

We believe a portion of the probes should be treated as third-party-induced rather than Redwood-native. Happy to share the full log if helpful.

— OrbitData SRE
[attachment: orbit-edge-ORB-20270212-231.log]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed SLO variance during failover window — request for tally rationale

Alex — thanks to OrbitData for the quick turn on logs. Laura and I dug into the traces and our SLO apportionment model; here's what we propose after cross-checking the probe sampling alignment: 

Summary of findings
- Sample alignment: 5 probes fell entirely inside the retry/failover window; 3 of those probes contained payloads that hit the older model variant and failed the binary probe success check.
- Attribution: The initial trigger was an OrbitData auth retry. However, our runtime's fallback behavior turned some retries into hard failures because the cached model variant did not accept the updated request framing. That means responsibility is split.

Proposed remediation
- Adjusted tally: mark the 3 probe failures as "partial degradation" in the customer SLA report rather than full outages. This reduces the calculated uptime impact by ~0.6 percentage points for the month. (Updated CSV attached: slo-tally-202702.csv)
- Credit option: offer a one-time pro-rated credit equal to 25% of the per-month SLA credit formula for the impacted period, or we can apply a formal maintenance exception if ACME prefers no credit on record.
- Operational fix: we will add a short-circuit in the fallback path so cached model variants accept the revised I/O framing when served during a region failover. ETA for the code change: 3 business days; production roll by next maintenance window.

Please let us know which remediation you prefer and whether you want the updated SLA line item (we can send a corrected PDF for procurement). If you accept the adjusted tally only, we will update the monthly report immediately and close the ticket.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-tally-202702.csv
